chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Ibn Muskān, from Muḥammad ibn Muḍārib, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a heap of wheat that had been plastered with clay: may I perform salat (prayer) on top of it? He said: Do not perform salat (prayer) on top of it. I said: But it is level like a roof. He said: Do not perform salat (prayer) upon it.
So the proper understanding of this report is that it indicates a kind of disapproval short of prohibition.

key_terms.السَّطْحِ: a roof or flat elevated surface
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: disapproval or reprehensibility in legal context
key_terms.كُدْسِ: a heap or pile, here referring to a heap of wheat

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) on a plastered heap of wheat?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of performing salat (prayer) on top of a plastered heap of wheat. The apparent prohibition in the report is understood here as indicating karāhah, meaning reprehensibility or disapproval, rather than absolute forbiddance.
